questions: Should the time values recorded for the plot be the absolute timestamps (as in the reference solution) or should they be relative to the start of the function (e.g., 0, 1, 2, ... seconds)?
Is the kurtosis computed using Fisher's definition (excess kurtosis, where normal distribution = 0) or Pearson's definition (where normal distribution = 3)?
Should the function handle negative intervals or non-integer intervals? The test includes intervals=0 but not negative.
Should the plot include any labels (title, x-axis, y-axis) or formatting, or is a bare plot with just the line acceptable?
If a KeyboardInterrupt occurs, should the function still return the Axes and kurtosis based on data collected so far, or raise an exception? The reference solution prints but continues.
Should the random seed be set only once at the start, or should it be reset per interval? The reference sets it once.
Is the delay of 1 second required to be exact (using time.sleep) or can it be approximate? The reference uses time.sleep(1).
Should the function close or reuse existing matplotlib figures? The reference creates a new figure with plt.figure() and also subplots.
